title: Timeseries reconciliation & per-model usage attribution correction
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description:
Summary:
Over the last three weeks ops and several customer tickets called out inconsistent token/embedding counts in the Console per-model breakdowns vs the billing ledger. Symptoms include: intermittent drops in historical timeseries (midnight to 06:00 UTC), duplicated spikes when backfills / replays happened, and model attribution mismatch when a request was proxied to a variant model. This ticket centralizes the engineering work to correct the analytics pipeline, enforce idempotent ingestion, and add an automated reconciliation that guarantees the Console charts align with the billing ledger within an audited tolerance window.

Observed root causes (investigation notes):
- Late events were being dropped by the streaming pipeline (Beam) due to an aggressive watermark (current max allowed lateness = 10s). Customers replaying logs or delayed Kafka partitions produced events with ingestion_timestamp older than the pipeline watermark, causing the hourly aggregators to skip them.
- Backfill job (ingest-replay service) wrote records with ingestion_ts instead of canonical_event_ts. The Console hourly rollups used ingestion_ts for bucket assignment while billing used canonical_event_ts, producing misaligned time buckets.
- Duplicate counting when a request was proxied: the proxy emitted both original and proxy events without a shared idempotency key; downstream dedup relied on approximate set cardinality which allowed doubles during partitions/resends.
- Per-model attribution used the request.model_name field which sometimes contained temporary alias names for routing. Billing uses pinned_model_id; Console used model_name, leading to mismatches in per-model cost allocation.

Proposed fixes (high level):
1) Streaming pipeline: increase watermark lateness to 5 minutes for the usage topic; add side-output tombstone for late-but-valid events so they can be sent to a backfill queue instead of being dropped.
2) Canonical timestamps: enforce canonical_event_ts at the producer boundary (Inference API + Dedicated edge) and change downstream aggregations to bucket by canonical_event_ts. Add schema enforcement in the ingestion gateway (jsonschema + validator).
3) Idempotency: require ingestion_id (UUID) for every meter event. Implement deterministic upsert in ClickHouse/aggregator (ReplaceMerge or materialized view with latest ingestion_id dedupe) so replays are safe.
4) Attribution normalization: add a mapping table (model_alias -> model_id) populated by model registry; aggregator will join to resolve pinned_model_id and use that for per-model breakdowns.
5) Reconciliation job: scheduled nightly job to compare Console aggregates vs billing ledger with per-tenant, per-model, per-hour granularity. Tolerances: <=0.5% token difference daily, <=1% for 95th percentile single-hour. Any >1% triggers PagerDuty.
6) Backfill tooling: build an idempotent rehydration job to reprocess the last 30 days of events into the corrected aggregation path. Backfill will run with canary subset of tenants first (internal+beta) then full run.

Acceptance criteria:
- Nightly reconciliation report runs and shows <0.5% daily token divergence for test tenants (internal) for 7 consecutive days.
- New ingestion schema enforced; producers without ingestion_id are rejected with clear error (400 + error_code METER_001).
- Console per-model charts use pinned_model_id and historical data aligns with billing ledger within tolerance after backfill.
- No data duplication observed in reprocessed windows (zero idempotency incidents in logs).

Artifacts / links:
- Confluence (design + runbook): https://company.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PLAT/pages/Usage+Timeseries+Reconciliation
- Design doc (schema & pipeline): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c-usageschema
- GH PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingestion/pull/612 (schema enforcement), https://github.com/redwood-inference/aggregator/pull/455 (dedupe + watermark changes)
- Staging reconciliation dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/usage-recon/reconciliation-staging
- PagerDuty runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Usage+Reconciliation+Runbook

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (today->+3 days): deploy schema enforcement on staging producers; run a dry-run ingestion that tags rejected events.
- Phase 1 (+3 to +7 days): deploy watermark and dedupe changes to streaming pipeline in staging; run reconciliation job and validate against staging billing ledger.
- Phase 2 (+8 to +14 days): canary backfill for internal tenants (5% of production) using backfill tool; monitor cost and chart differences.
- Phase 3 (+15 to +21 days): full backfill and prod rollout with alerting enabled.

Safety/observability:
- Add metric: meter_events_late_count, meter_events_deduped_count, meter_events_rejected_schema_count.
- New dashboards to track per-tenant reconciliation delta (tokens, calls, embeddings).
- PagerDuty escalation if any tenant exceeds defined tolerances for 2 consecutive runs.

Open trade-offs / questions:
- Watermark lateness of 5 minutes may increase state retention and memory usage in Beam; alternative is to rely on backfill queue only, but that increases complexity of confirming final completeness for hourly charts. Engineering prefers 5-minute lateness to reduce frequency of backfills.
- ClickHouse upsert semantics add load; if throughput impact is large we may need to move dedupe to pre-aggregator tier (Redis bloom + compacted Kafka topic).

Estimated workstreams and owners:
- Ingestion schema & gateway validation: Miguel Torres (owner) + backend (ENG-7033)
- Streaming pipeline watermark & side-output: Priya Desai (owner) + streaming team (ENG-7010)
- Aggregator dedupe & attribution join: Arun Patel (owner) + storage team (ENG-7055)
- Reconciliation job & dashboards: Sofia Nguyen (owner) + analytics (ENG-7099)
- Backfill tool orchestration: DevOps runbook + SRE (ENG-7182)

This ticket will be split into sub-issues for each owner for tracking. See updates for ongoing progress and links to incremental PRs and tests.
updates: 2026-02-22: Initial investigation complete. Confirmed watermark and timestamp mismatch as primary causes (Sofia).
2026-02-25: Prototype change to use canonical_event_ts in a shadow aggregator completed. Shadow results show alignment with billing for 3 internal tenants (Sofia + Arun).
2026-03-02: GH PR ingestions/schema enforcement opened (#612). Waiting on reviewer feedback from Priya.
2026-03-05: Streaming change to emit late events to backfill queue merged in staging; observed ~0.2% of events classified as late in the last 48h (Priya).
2026-03-10: Aggregator dedupe PR (#455) merged to staging. Early benchmarks show ~8% CPU overhead on aggregator workers under 95th p95 load (Arun).
2026-03-12: Nightly reconciliation run on staging shows 0.12% daily divergence for internal tenants; enabling canary backfill next (Sofia).
acceptance_criteria: Nightly reconciliation job exists and runs successfully with reports persisted for 30 days.
Per-tenant per-model daily divergence <= 0.5% for internal canary tenants for 7 days.
Console per-model charts reflect pinned_model_id post-backfill and no later regressions for 14 days.
Idempotency enforced at ingestion (replays do not create duplicates).
implementation_notes: Add ingestion_id in schema and mark it required; producers must roll forward clients within a 2-week window.
Use ReplaceMerge or materialized view pattern in ClickHouse to support idempotent upserts; test on small partition first.
Add telemetry tags tenant_id and model_id consistently across pipeline (make them required labels).
Ensure reconciliation job compares canonical_event_ts buckets with billing ledger and writes discrepancy records to a dedicated table for audit.
